headline: Bangladesh faces over 3,000 MW load shedding daily, rural areas hit hardest amid fuel crisis
summary: Despite recent electricity price hikes, the Power Development Board (PDB) struggles to pay power plants, leading to severe fuel shortages and daily load shedding exceeding 3,000 MW, with rural areas disproportionately affected.
details: Bangladesh is experiencing daily load shedding exceeding 3,000 megawatts, with Monday seeing a peak of 3,757 MW. Rural areas are disproportionately affected, enduring hours of power outages, while urban centers like Dhaka face fewer disruptions.

The Power Development Board (PDB) is struggling to pay power plants, with nearly BDT 50,000 crore owed, contributing to a severe fuel crisis. This includes persistent gas shortages and reluctance to increase production from costly oil-fired plants.

Experts note that despite 12 wholesale and 14 retail price hikes over the last decade, the government built numerous power plants without securing fuel. Many of these plants remain idle but still incur capacity charges, adding to PDB's financial burden.

PDB officials state that the benefits of the recent price increases, which saw wholesale rates rise by 19.85% and retail by 16.68% in June, will take two months to materialize. They expect new arrears to halt and old debts to be paid in phases.

Despite a generation capacity of 29,000 MW, Bangladesh supplied only 12,500 MW against a demand of 16,262 MW during peak load shedding, leaving over half the capacity idle. Gas-fired production is below 4,000 MW, and increasing oil-fired generation is deemed too expensive.

Coal-fired power plants are now the primary reliance, but three major ones face issues. Payra power plant's output was halved due to maintenance and over BDT 9,000 crore in arrears, while another Patuakhali plant has a coal shortage. Adani's plant in Jharkhand also reduced production due to storm-related coal supply disruptions.

PDB held an online meeting with power plants, instructing Payra and Adani's plants to increase supply. Adani's power plant informed Prothom Alo that coal supply is expected to normalize between August 11 night and August 12 morning.

The impact is severe in rural areas; Fenny experiences 35% load shedding in factories and a 15% deficit in rural electricity. Residents in Netrokona's Purbadhala report receiving power for only 5 hours a day, with supply at 59 MW against a demand of 158 MW. Some parts of Habiganj face up to 12 hours of outages.

headline: 111 killed in 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia, injuring 87
summary: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake devastated western Colombia, collapsing buildings and trapping many under rubble. The new administration faces its first major crisis as rescue efforts intensify.
details: At least 111 people have been killed and 87 injured after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia yesterday. The quake caused widespread destruction, knocking down buildings across several cities and trapping many under rubble.

The US Geological Survey reported the quake struck at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar in Choco province. Despite being a sparsely populated area, the tremors were felt in major cities nationwide.

The disaster marks the first major crisis for President Abelardo De La Espriella, who was sworn in just days prior. He declared a national state of emergency, deploying all government capabilities to protect lives and assist affected communities.
In Manizales, a tower of the beloved cathedral collapsed, and many buildings sustained damage, paralyzing traffic. Residents are hesitant to return home due to fears of aftershocks.

Cali, one of Colombia's largest cities, saw over two dozen structures collapse, with people still trapped. Mayor Alejandro Eder requested disaster teams from Bogota and Medellin to support the ongoing rescue operations.
Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi confirmed injuries and significant damage in the provincial capital, Quibdo. She also issued warnings to residents about potential aftershocks.
